summary.text: Jake Ellzey is the Republican incumbent U.S. Representative for Texas's 6th Congressional District. A retired Navy pilot, he later worked as a commercial airline pilot and served on the Texas Veterans Commission and in the Texas House before winning a 2021 special election to Congress, where he sits on the Appropriations and Small Business committees.

paragraphs.text: Born in Perryton, Texas, and raised on his family's ranch, according to his official biography.
Earned a bachelor's degree in political science from the United States Naval Academy in 1992.

Served in the U.S. Navy from 1992 to 2012. His official biography says he flew helicopters and later F-14 and F/A-18 fighter aircraft, deployed nine times including five combat tours, and ended his career as Air Boss aboard the USS Ronald Reagan.
After the Navy, worked as a military contractor in Afghanistan, a small business owner and a commercial airline pilot, and served as a commissioner of the Texas Veterans Commission.
Ran in the 2018 Republican primary for Texas's 6th District and placed second, according to Wikipedia.
Elected to the Texas House of Representatives (District 10) in 2020 and took office in January 2021.
Won the July 27, 2021 special general runoff for Texas's 6th District over Susan Wright and took office July 30, 2021, succeeding the late Rep. Ronald Wright.

In the 119th Congress he serves on the Appropriations Committee (Defense; Interior, Environment, and Related Agencies; and Labor, Health and Human Services, Education, and Related Agencies subcommittees) and the Small Business Committee.
According to his official biography, he lives in Ellis County with his wife, Shelby, and their two children.
